8: The seven products in this experiment were prepared from nine traditional aromatic rice cultivars of West Bengal, with Dudeshwar, a non-aromatic cultivar, included as the control. Each product was laid out in a completely randomised design with three replications and repeated over two years. The two years were analysed jointly as a pooled design, with year as a fixed effect and cultivar as a random effect. The model was Yijk = mu + Yi + Tj + (YT)ij + eijk, the degrees of freedom being year 1, cultivar 9, year by cultivar 9, error 40 and total 59.
9: The results are presented in two parts. Part A covers the four cooked products, table rice, kichidi, pulao and payash, and Part B the three processed products, popped rice, puffed rice and flattened rice. Within each part every attribute is presented once for the group, with all the products of that part assembled in one table and one figure, both reporting the means pooled over the two years. Means were separated at the 5 per cent level and are reported with letter groupings; a cultivar is deemed to differ from the control only where the two share no letter. Throughout, ** denotes significance at 1 per cent, * at 5 per cent and NS non-significance. Since a high value is favourable for certain attributes and a low value for others, each cultivar is compared with the control in the direction appropriate to that attribute.
10: Each part concludes with a composite quality score index, a verification of the weights of that index by principal component analysis, a cluster analysis of the cultivar and product combinations, and a conclusion. Tables and figures are numbered consecutively through both parts.

The year effect was significant in 1 product and the year by cultivar interaction in 1, so that the ranking of the cultivars was largely stable from one year to the next. 22: Discussion. Amylose content determines the firmness and discreteness of the cooked grain: a higher content yields a firmer, drier grain that retains its shape, and a lower content a softer, stickier one. Amylose is deposited by granule-bound starch synthase I at the Waxy locus, and cultivars differ in the allele they carry. Cooking disorganises the granule but does not alter the quantity of amylose present.
23: Earlier work is largely concordant. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that apparent amylose governs eating and processing behaviour; Tian et al. (2018) that crystallinity and digestibility decline without any change in amylose; Cheng et al. (2019) that heat and moisture reconstitute the matrix into a firmer gel; and Devi and Badwaik (2022) that amylose accounts for most of the varietal difference in cooking behaviour. The most favourable entry varied between products, Kalojira and Tulaipanjii each ranking highest in one product or another, so that selection is contingent upon the product concerned.

29: Discussion. Starch constitutes the energy-supplying fraction of the grain and the basis of its texture; a higher value indicates a well-filled endosperm and good recovery of the edible fraction. Starch content is contingent upon the efficiency with which assimilate was translocated into the endosperm during grain filling, and in the prepared product it is further modified by the loss of low-molecular-weight material and by the water imbibed during cooking.
30: This is consistent with previous studies. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that starch constitutes approximately nine tenths of milled rice on a dry weight basis; Tian et al. (2018) that the residual starch is swollen and less crystalline; Iqbal et al. (2021) that restructured starch resists digestion; and Cheng et al. (2019) that the extent of starch gelatinisation governs texture and digestibility. The leading cultivar varied with the product, Kalonunia, Kataribhog, Lal Badshabhog and Radhunipagal ranking highest in turn, so that no single recommendation covers the group on this attribute.

36: Discussion. Protein constitutes the principal nutritional contribution of rice after energy and additionally firms the cooked grain through disulphide bonding. The greater part of the protein is glutelin sequestered in protein bodies beneath the aleurone, and the quantity is contingent upon the nitrogen translocated into the grain during filling. Cooking does not alter it.
37: Published work is concordant. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that total protein is unaltered by hydrothermal treatment; Cheng et al. (2019) that disulphide cross-links elevate firmness; Akter et al. (2025) that protein rose from 6.68 to 9.42 per cent following treatment; and Iqbal et al. (2021) that the protein network governs enzyme access to starch. The leading position was shared between Gobindabhog, Kalojira, Kalonunia and Radhunipagal, so that selection on this attribute must be made product by product.

43: Discussion. Soluble protein is the fraction remaining extractable, and therefore digestible, after cooking; a higher value indicates that heat has not aggregated the protein. Heat ruptures the protein bodies and subsequently cross-links the liberated chains through disulphide bonds, thereby reducing the extractable fraction, and cultivars richer in cysteine forfeit more.
44: The same pattern has been reported previously. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that solubility alters while total protein does not; Cheng et al. (2019) that cross-linking reduces the extractable fraction; Kabir et al. (2025) that treatment modifies the association between protein and bound phenolics; and Roy et al. (2019) that solubility declines as steaming and soaking become more severe. Gobindabhog, Radhunipagal and Tulaipanjii each headed the ranking in a different product, so that this attribute cannot determine the selection for the group as a whole.

50: Discussion. Lipid is localised in the germ and aleurone and carries the fat-soluble vitamins and the aroma compounds. A higher content is preferable, subject to the qualification that excess lipid curtails shelf life. Lipid is stored as triacylglycerol in the germ and aleurone, so that the value reflects both the extent of these tissues in the cultivar and the degree of milling.
51: Earlier reports corroborate this finding. Muchlisyiyah et al. (2023) determined that lipid resides in the germ and aleurone and oxidises readily; Hu et al. (2019) that the movement of water within the kernel displaces the lipid-bearing tissues; Devi and Badwaik (2022) that traditional cultivars differ widely in proximate composition; and Oliveira et al. (2026) that milling is the principal route by which the outer layers are lost. No single cultivar proved superior across all the products: Dudeshwar, Kalojira and Radhunipagal ranked highest in different ones, so that the decision is contingent upon the product concerned.
